name: Cutting Teeth

summary: In the Valley of Trials, fresh recruits face a first test against mottled boars. Overseer Gornek sends aspiring warriors and spellcasters to thin the boars around the cactus dirt farms, where they can prove their fighting skill and readiness to serve the Horde.

sections.title: A Measure of Backbone
sections.body: The Valley of Trials leaves little room for grand dreams. Young recruits may imagine hunting great beasts in the Barrens or winning glory on a battlefield, but overseer Gornek begins with the farms. Thinning the mottled boars is a grounded test of a recruit’s first skills with a weapon or spell. It shows whether they can face a wild attacker and have the sense to survive their first skirmish.

sections.title: Taming the Red Dust
sections.body: Feral swine roam the red desert settlement’s dirt farms north and northeast of camp. They root through cactus patches and threaten the few supplies grown in Durotar’s harsh soil. Sending aspirants to clear them keeps local pests in check while shaping young orcs and trolls into defenders of the new nation.

faq.q: Why does Gornek send recruits after boars instead of bigger beasts?
faq.answer: Gornek sends recruits after boars because the Horde needs them alive. The Barrens hold mighty kodo and predators, but an untried recruit sent against them could be needlessly killed. Boars offer a sound test of basic fighting skill without throwing lives away.

faq.q: Where are the mottled boars located?
faq.answer: Mottled boars root through scrub and dirt farms north and northeast of the central clearing in the Valley of Trials.

faq.q: What is the significance of the phrase 'cutting teeth'?
faq.answer: “Cutting teeth” means gaining a first practical experience in a craft or calling. For an aspiring Horde defender, it means leaving training dummies and idle talk behind and drawing blood in a fight for survival.
Gornek assigns the trial. He is an overseer at the heart of the Valley of Trials, where he evaluates and directs new recruits entering Durotar’s training grounds.

faq.q: Does this complete the training in the Valley of Trials?
faq.answer: No. Gornek warns that fighting boars is only a warm-up. More dangerous challenges follow, including facing humanoid intruders and gathering vital valley resources.

faq.q: Why do the boars pose a problem in the valley?
faq.answer: Feral boars roam the local dirt farms and brush patches, endangering workers and eating the few hardy crops, such as cactus fruit, that sustain the encampment.

angles.text: Every young champion who enters Durotar starts in the dirt, proving that the Horde’s future rests on their blood and sweat, not unearned prestige.
Orcish culture prizes practical survival and martial honor. Even culling boars is a sacred first step into adulthood and service to Thrall’s new nation.
As the Darkspear tribe rebuilds alongside its orc allies, young troll scouts and mystics prove their self-reliance among Durotar’s unforgiving predators.
